questions.question: Mention two features that make hospitality services perishable.
questions.solution_html:
• Intangibility and Simultaneity: Hospitality services are experienced and consumed
  • at the same time they are delivered, making them perishable.
  • Time-sensitive: Hospitality services have a limited timeframe for delivery and
  • consumption.

questions.question: Explain the concept of franchising in hotel chains using an Indian brand example.
questions.solution_html:
• Franchising is a business model where a hotel chain (the franchisor) grants
  • permission to an individual or company (the franchisee) to operate a hotel using its
  • brand name, logo, and business model. The franchisee pays fees and royalties to the
  • franchisor in exchange for access to its brand reputation, marketing support, and
  • operational expertise.
  • Indian Brand Example: Taj Hotels
  • Taj Hotels, a renowned Indian hospitality brand, has expanded its presence through
  • franchising. Under a franchise agreement, Taj Hotels allows independent hotel
  • owners to operate properties using the Taj brand name and standards. The franchisee
  • benefits from Taj's strong brand reputation, global marketing reach, and operational
  • expertise, while Taj Hotels earns revenue through franchise fees and royalties.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: expertise, while Taj Hotels earns revenue through franchise fees and royalties.

questions.question: Discuss how guest expectations vary across cultures.
questions.solution_html:
• Guest expectations can differ significantly across cultures, influenced by their cultural
  • background, personal values, and past experiences.
  • Communication Styles
  • Direct vs. Indirect- Guests from low-context cultures (e.g., USA, Germany) prefer
  • direct and clear communication, while those from high-context cultures (e.g., Japan
  • India) may rely more on non-verbal cues and implicit messages.
  • Personal Space
  • Proximity: Guests from cultures that value personal space may prefer more
  • distance during interactions, while those from cultures with closer proximity norms
  • may feel more comfortable with less personal space.
  • Time and Punctuality- Service Expectations:- Level of Service
  • Food Preferences- Social Interactions

questions.question: Describe the line of authority in a full-service hotel.
questions.solution_html:
• The line of authority in a full-service hotel typically follows a hierarchical structure
  • with clear reporting relationships and responsibilities.
  • General Manager (GM)
  • The GM is the head of the hotel and oversees all operations. They are responsible for
  • setting strategic goals, managing budgets, and ensuring guest satisfaction.
  • Department Heads
  • Report to the GM and oversee specific departments, such as
  • Front Office Manager
  • Food and Beverage Manager
  • Executive Housekeeper
  • Sales and Marketing Manager
  • Human Resources Manager
  • Supervisors/Team Leaders
  • Line Staff
  • Frontline employees who interact directly with guests, such as
  • Front desk agents
  • Housekeeping staff
  • Servers and bartenders
  • Bell staff and concierges

questions.question: Explain the importance of night auditing.
questions.solution_html:
• A night audit is a critical process in the hospitality industry, particularly in hotels. It
  • involves reviewing and reconciling financial transactions, room occupancy, and other
  • operational data from the previous day. The night auditor typically performs this task
  • during the overnight shift.
  • Financial Accuracy
  • Revenue Management
  • Operational Efficiency
